questions.question: Describe SALT and explain why it was built near Sutherland.
questions.expected_answer: SALT, the Southern African Large Telescope, is the largest single light telescope in the southern half of the world. It is a reflecting telescope with a main mirror about eleven metres across, made of ninety-one six-sided pieces kept lined up by computers, so it can collect light from extremely faint, distant objects. It was built near Sutherland because the hills are high, the air is dry with few clouds, and it is far from city lights, so the sky is very dark.

questions.question: What is MeerKAT, and why is there a radio quiet zone around it?
questions.expected_answer: MeerKAT is a radio telescope near Carnarvon in the Karoo, made of sixty-four dishes, each about thirteen and a half metres across, built mostly by South Africans. A computer combines their signals as if they were one gigantic dish. It collects faint radio waves from space, so signals from cell phones, radios and microwaves nearby could drown them out. That is why the area is protected by law as a radio quiet zone.

questions.question: What is the SKA, and why is South Africa a good place for big telescopes?
questions.expected_answer: The SKA, the Square Kilometre Array, is an international project to build the largest radio telescope in the world, with more dishes added to MeerKAT in the Karoo and thousands of antennas in Australia. South Africa is a good place because, from the southern half of the world, we have the best view of the centre of the Milky Way and the Magellanic Clouds, and the Karoo is dark, dry, high and radio quiet.
